title: AI Agents, Meet Test Driven Development
talk_summary: The talk argues that reliable AI products come from TDD-style experimentation, evaluation, monitoring, and continuous improvement, not just better models. It demos an SEO agent with a writer/editor LLM-judge loop and recommends logging, fallbacks, caching, staging, and decoupled AI deployments.

takeaways.what_they_do: They build a dataset of hundreds of examples, ideally ground-truth from subject-matter experts, and evaluate workflows against it; if no ground truth, use an LLM judge.
takeaways.evidence_quote: create a data set of hundreds of examples that you're going to test your models and workflows against

takeaways.what_they_do: They pass a writer draft to an LLM editor judge, feed feedback through memory, and loop until quality criteria or max iterations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the first draft is passed to the editor which is an llm based judge
takeaways.numbers: demo latency ~118s; ~300s with more evaluation loops

takeaways.what_they_do: They cache repeated queries so the same request does not call an expensive LLM repeatedly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if your system is handling some repeat queries caching can drastically reduce costs and improve latency

takeaways.what_they_do: They require retries and fallback logic to another model to survive API outages.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to have retries you need to have fallback logic to prevent outages

takeaways.what_they_do: They log all LLM calls with inputs, outputs, and latency, and add guardrails that check internal workflow nodes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to log all llm calls you need to track all of those inputs and outputs and the latency

takeaways.what_they_do: They version-control prompts and deploy AI changes separately from app deployments, using staging to catch regressions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: decouple your deployments from your scheduled app deployment schedule
